2. The relevant fact in short for disposal of the Rule is that Jatindra Chandra Urang, the father of the opposite party Nos.1(ka)-1(gha) as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous (pre-emption) Case No. 118 of 1985 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against 9(nine) opposite-parties including the petition-er (vendee) in the Court of Sub-Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur on the averments that the suit land originally belonged to Hemba Urang Hemba Dhangar and Debra Urang ©. Debra Dhangar in 8 annas share each; that Debra Urang had purchased lands in SA Khatian No. 255 and CS Khatian No. 71 from Gopal Dhangar, khatian No. 341 (CS Khatian No. 125)/SA khatian No. 242 (CS Khatian No. 65) from one Kalicharan Dhangar; that while jointly owning and possessing the properties described in schedule the said Hembra Urang died leaving Rabindra Chandra Urang, the opposite party No.2 as his legal heir and Debra Urang died leaving Jatindra Chandra Urang as his legal heir. After the death of said Hembra Urang and Debra Urang Rabindra Chandra Urang and Jatindra Chandra Urang have been owning and possessing the properties jointly without partition by metes and bounds and in this way Jatindra Chandra Urang along with Rabindra Chandra Urang became owner of the case Khatians and holdings by way of inheritance and purchase; that opposite party No. 2, Rabindra Chandra Urang secretly transferred the case land to opposite party No. 1, Md Shamsuddin by executing sale deed No. 8360 dated 30-11-76 corresponding to 14th Agrahayan, 1383 BS without serving any notice of transfer upon the pre-emptor applicant under section 89 of the Act, who being a stranger to the case land; that the pre-emptor-applicant came to know about the transfer of the case land on 1-2-77 for the first time and then he rushed to the Sub-Registrar Office at Shreepur and obtained the certified copy of the sale deed No.8360 dated on 24-2-77 and filed the case for pre-emption. 

 9. Drawing my attention to the paragraph No. 4 of the application under Order 6 Rule 17 read with section 151 CPC Mr Majid submits that pre-emptor-Jatindra Chandra Urang lost his right of pre-emption by selling his entire share of the suit Khatians but the Courts below without considering this aspect of the case most illegally arrived at a finding that the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 is a co-sharer to the case land. Mr Majid further submits that pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 approached before the Court with unclean hands stating that his father Debra Urang died leaving behind the pre-emptor as sole heir but the case record shows that the father of the pre-emptor-opposite party died leaving behind his 3(three) sons including the pre-emptor. 

 "So from the above documents it has been proved that the OP No. 1 is the co-sharer of one of the suit Khatians and holdings. But it appears from the disputed deed that the lands of several holdings and Khatians have been transferred: The petitioners are the co-sharers by inheritance in the suit plots and holdings. On the other hand, the predecessor of the OP No. 1 was co-sharer by purchase in one khatian among the suit Khatians and holdings. According to section 96 of the SA & T Act co-sharer by inheritance would get first preference other than by purchase. Since the petitioners are the co-sharers by inheritance is the suit Khatians and holdings that is why petitioners would get preference over the OP No. 1." 

 17. The above quoted evidence clearly shows that pre-emptee Shamsuddin (vendee) is a co-sharer to the case land of SA Khatian No. 242 by way of inheritance. 

 18. It is found that the pre-emptee-petitioner to prove his case examined 2(two) witnesses and exhibited a series of documents including the SA Khatian No. 242. The pre-emptee-purchaser Shamsuddin himself was examined as OPW-1, who in his deposition stated that he purchased the case land by registered deed No. 8360 dated 31-11-1976 within the full knowledge of the pre-emptor. This witness also stated that his father Rajab Ali purchased 1.40 acres of land of the case khatian from one Ram Urang and others and proved the original deed No. 4380 as 'Exhibit-Kha' dated 17-4-1942.
